day_shape: Second tanker reported struck in Strait of Hormuz with IRGC claiming mine strikes and warning darkened ships will be treated as hostile, Houthi attack on Riyadh airport killed 12 and wounded 300+, and Iran called US response to its seven Hormuz conditions 'insufficient'.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz tanker incidents
threads.summary: UKMTO reported a tanker damaged near Sohar, Oman, while IRGC-affiliated Defa Press and IRIB claimed a second super-tanker struck a sea mine south of the Strait after disabling navigation systems. The IRGC navy commander said any vessel in the Strait with navigation systems switched off would be treated as hostile.

threads.label: Iran-US Hormuz negotiations stall
threads.summary: Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaee said the US response to Iran's seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz was 'insufficient', per Iranian state media. Rezaee separately told Press TV that the CENTCOM commander was leading smuggling operations off Oman's coast.

threads.label: Houthi Riyadh airport attack fallout
threads.summary: The Houthis claimed responsibility for Saturday's attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, which Times of Israel and Jerusalem Post reported killed at least 12 and wounded over 300. European leaders, the UN and Mecca Joint Defense Agreement members condemned the strike; Defa Press claimed Yemeni forces also halted flights at Dammam's King Fahd airport.

threads.label: IDF Gaza operations and Kamal Adwan footage
threads.summary: The IDF released footage and an interrogation it said showed armed Hamas operatives at Kamal Adwan Hospital, and reported a 24-hour recap of strikes on a Daraj Tuffah command centre, a rocket launch site and three weapons storage facilities. The IDF also said it eliminated Nukhba platoon commander Hisham Jamal Muhammad Abu Ghala, linked to the Kissufim raid on October 7.

threads.label: Lebanon/Hezbollah interdictions
threads.summary: The IDF fired interceptors at suspicious aerial targets over southern Lebanon with no sirens sounded, per Jerusalem Post. Lebanese forces seized hundreds of kilograms of explosives from a vehicle at a Bekaa Valley checkpoint and arrested two people linked to Hezbollah.
